mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently signals an accommodative monetary policy that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 9.0%, it signals a weakening labor market and potential economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and retail sales indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production below 95.0 signals supply constraints that lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0 during late-cycle expansions, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL above 225.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to central bank tightening and reduced real returns over the next 20 trading days.
